Chapter 7: Navigating Obstacles—Common Challenges and Skillful Responses
As you dive deeper into your practice, it's only natural to run into a few roadblocks—sometimes from within, and sometimes from the world around you. But here’s the thing: these challenges aren’t proof you’re failing. In fact, they’re really just opportunities to learn, grow, and understand yourself better.
So, let’s take a look at some of the most common difficulties people face, and how you can meet them with a little more wisdom and patience.
One of the most frequent hurdles? Restlessness or maybe even boredom during practice. If you’re used to a world full of constant stimulation, the mind can really resist stillness. You might find yourself distracted, your thoughts wandering every which way. But both Yoga and Vipassana have some beautiful guidance for this.
First, try gentle persistence. Instead of forcing yourself to concentrate, approach your mind with curiosity. Notice that restlessness for what it is—a passing sensation, just like a wave rising and falling.
You can also bring a little variety into your practice. Mix things up with some physical postures, a bit of breathwork, or a few minutes of meditation. Switching it up keeps your mind engaged and your body comfortable.
And here’s something really important: talk to yourself kindly. When frustration pops up, treat yourself the way you’d treat a good friend. Acknowledge that you’re having a tough time, but don’t beat yourself up over it.
Another challenge that can show up is emotional turbulence. Sometimes, as you spend more time looking inward, old wounds or fears may float to the surface. Instead of trying to avoid these feelings, both Yoga and Vipassana encourage you to meet them with acceptance. That might mean using your breath and movement to help release tension, or simply observing your emotions as they come and go—without trying to push them away or hold onto them.
Of course, life throws external challenges at us too. Maybe you’re short on time, your environment isn’t supportive, or you have a mountain of responsibilities. This is where a little flexibility goes a long way. If you can’t do a long session, shorten it or break it into smaller pieces throughout the day. And don’t hesitate to seek out communities—online or in person—where you can share your experiences and get a little encouragement.
Above all, remember: obstacles are a natural part of the journey. Each difficulty you face, as long as you approach it with awareness and patience, becomes its own kind of teacher.
Over time, the skills you build—resilience, equanimity, and greater self-understanding—start to show up in every part of your life.
So, next time you run into a challenge, try meeting it with curiosity and kindness. Who knows? You just might discover something new about yourself along the way.
